coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Mission Bay Open Space Parcel P23
names: Mission Bay Open Space Parcel P23
search_aliases: P23 -- landscaped plaza and lawn (north of the pavilion, toward Chase Center)
record.summary: A landscaped lawn and plaza between Illinois Street and Terry A. Francois Boulevard, extending toward the Chase Center roundabout and next to a pavilion (not the Mission Creek Park Pavilion, which is about 800 m to the north-west); per Pier & Point's own reading of satellite imagery, real landscaped/paved open land; its outline was traced by hand by Pier & Point as the open ground left between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes, not taken from a surveyed parcel boundary. OCII's own September 2023 Mission Bay Parks Open Space transition presentation lists 'P23' among the parcels the Port of San Francisco will manage (not among the 'when built' parcels); that presentation is a plan and does not say whether the area was built. SocketSite (April 2019) calls the combined P23/P24 area 'Mariposa Bayfront Park'; no source gives this lawn's own formal name. OCII's November 14, 2024 update map labels 'P23 & P24' with the colour its legend gives as a completed park; the deck gives no completion date.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- real landscaped/paved open land per Esri satellite imagery, outlined as the open ground left between the official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes and divided at seams chosen by hand by Pier & Point, rather than a surveyed parcel boundary. Operator: the Port of San Francisco per OCII's Sept 2023 transition presentation ('Port will manage P18, P21, P23 & P24'); SocketSite (April 2019) calls the combined P23/P24 area 'Mariposa Bayfront Park'; no source gives this lawn's own formal name. The remaining ~5,785 sqm of the original fragment (the building-hugging plaza strip, the panhandle, and P24's own dropped horns) is deliberately left off the map, pending further review of whether it is a separate plan parcel. DataSF's Assessor layer has active lot 3940002 (MB-RA|P zoning, active, 4,806 m2) near this park: 57% of this drawing lies inside it and the drawing covers 80% of the lot; the drawing and the lot overlap only in part, so the lot is not this park's own and the drawing is kept. Since 2026-10-12 the outline stops at the edge of Assessor lot 3940003 (409/499 Illinois Street), which overlapped it by 2,032 m2; that strip is part of the lot, not of this drawing.
notes.digitized_from: Outlined as the open ground left between DataSF's official street lines and neighbouring mapped shapes around the UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision / 499 Illinois St / Chase Center area (one piece of 19,181.78 sqm before cutting). Pier & Point split that piece in three at its two natural narrow points (lat 37.7658 and 37.76665) and then combined parts by hand: P23 is the north part (the lawn wedge by the Chase Center roundabout) with its thin building-hugging 'panhandle' dropped, plus the part of the middle piece (the plaza) that lies east of the line where the lawn narrows into that panhandle, extended south. Not taken from a surveyed parcel.
notes.why_no_real_parcel: Open space with no Assessor lot of its own: lot 3940002 was compared and does not match (see the accuracy note).

open_questions: The April 2019 SocketSite article names the combined P23/P24 area 'Mariposa Bayfront Park' -- not to be confused with Mariposa Park, OCII's own official P26 per its current open-space page (listed separately from P23/P24; see the open questions on Pier & Point's record for P26, the landscaped wedge at the 16th/3rd/Owens St interchange, for a related P26 label conflict). Not reconciled here, only noted so the two 'Mariposa'-named places aren't conflated.

No source names this specific lawn/plaza or gives its own completion date. SocketSite (April 22, 2019) described the P23/P24 open space as "yet to be completed" and "expected to be completed by the end of this year" (an expected date), and OCII's November 2024 map points its "P23 & P24" label at an area coloured as "COMPLETED PARK"; OCII's September 2023 presentation says only that the Port "will manage" P23 (a plan).

By Pier & Point's reading of the map it sits adjacent to the Chase Center arena (SocketSite, April 22, 2019: "slated to be completed this August", an expected date) and to the UCSF Wayne and Gladys Valley Center for Vision / 499 Illinois St area, but no source ties this landscaped area's own completion to either project.

Whether OCII's own current numbering scheme still uses 'P23' for exactly this footprint was not independently confirmed -- OCII's current public Mission Bay South open-space page (sfocii.org/projects/mission-bay-south/open-space) does not list a P23 at all among the parcels it names (P1, P2, P3, P5, P6, P26).

The April 2019 SocketSite article says only that the P23/P24 open space had 'yet to be completed' and was expected to be completed by the end of 2019; it does not say construction had started, so the 2019-04 milestone is 'planned', not 'under construction'.
